name: The Crooked Root
world: one clearing in an old deciduous wood, dominated by the exposed crooked root of a great tree -- a thick elbow of wood arching out of the earth with a sheltered hollow beneath it. Around it: leaf litter and acorns, a flat grey stone, a hollow of curled ferns, a forked birch, and a low branch overhanging the middle
palette: russet and ochre leaf litter, warm mid-brown bark, mossy greens, and in winter a cold blue-white snow over all of it with the browns showing through
light: bright, low, raking daylight through bare or thinning branches, throwing long tree-shadows across the clearing floor. Autumn mornings and frosty winter middays. Never lantern-lit and never night
recurring: the great crooked root with its elbow-shaped bend and the hollow underneath
the fern hollow, ferns curled like small closed umbrellas
the low branch over the middle of the clearing
acorns and hazelnuts on the ground
forbidden: paper lanterns or hung lights, which belong to Lantern Valley
night scenes or dusk; this clearing is seen by day
water larger than a puddle or a thaw-trickle
notes: Nibs and Tilly share one clearing across two books, and the landmarks are
load-bearing: Tilly's whole story is that she has every hiding place
mapped, and a map of a place that looks different each book is worth
nothing. The crooked root is named in both titles' worth of prose and has
to be recognisably the same object.
